newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan plans T$40 bln loan for zone development.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan plans T$40 bln loan for zone development.

text.p: Taiwan's economics ministry said on Friday it plans to ask other government offices to jointly offer T$40 billion worth of low-cost loans for the private sector to develop industrial-commercial zones.

"Our ministry just completed a proposal to ask the cabinet's Development Fund and Mid- and Long-term Fund to jointly offer T$40 billion worth of funds to help finance the development of industrial-commercial zones," a ministry official told Reuters.
"We have reached initial agreement with the two funds, and now we need only the final approval from the cabinet," he said.
The 10-year loan will include two parts, with the first part worth T$5 billion and jointly offered by the two funds with an annual interest rate of 6.5 percent, the official said.
The second part, worth T$35 billion and offered by the Mid- and Long-term Fund, will bear a rate of 7.5-7.6 percent, he said.
"The T$40 billion loan is designed to finance the first eight such projects that are expected to start construction by the end of this year," the official said.

So far, 39 interested companies have applied to convert either farm or industrial land into such industrial-commercial zones, and the economics ministry has granted initial approvals on 19 projects, he said.
Such zones will include shopping malls, warehouses, commercial service centres, software and product processing units, he said.
"In the future, we plan to offer more such loans to finance other projects other than the first eight projects," the official said.
